Let’s break down the SVG path data.  

The path contains two arc commands (`A`), both with the same radius values (8.30, 8.30), and both arcs are drawn with the large-arc-flag 1 and sweep-flag 0.  

The first arc:  
`M 26.95,11.95 A 8.30,8.30 322.18 1,0 13.83,22.13`  
This draws an arc from (26.95,11.95) to (13.83,22.13) with rx=ry=8.30, so it’s a circular arc (same x and y radius means it’s part of a circle, not an ellipse).  

The second arc:  
`A 8.30,8.30 322.18 1,0 26.95,11.95`  
This draws an arc from (13.83,22.13) back to (26.95,11.95) with the same radius and flags.  

Since both arcs have the same radii and form a closed path, together they make a full circle (two symmetric arcs completing a circle).  

Looking at the options, the only one matching a circle is (A).  

Final answer: (A)
